text:
Abstract
We assessed whether GEO accessions GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same record. Using GEO-targeted tools, we queried both the Series (GSE) and curated DataSet (GDS) namespaces and resolved each accession to its internal Entrez UID and FTP directory. The GSE309890 Series record (UID 200309890) returned complete metadata for an Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 RNA-seq study with 6 samples, platform GPL24659, and one supplementary file (FPKMs CSV) in its FTP directory. In contrast, GDS309890 resolved to a GDS accession (UID 309890) and an expected FTP directory path, but its summary metadata fields were empty and the GDS-specific FTP directory did not exist, with no supplementary files registered. These outcomes indicate the two accessions are not the same entity: GSE309890 is an active Series containing the study’s processed expression matrix, whereas GDS309890 is a curated DataSet accession that, as of the queried state, carries no accessible files or populated metadata. This distinction matters for data retrieval and reuse: to obtain processed expression values for this study, users must use the GSE-level FTP links; the GDS entry does not currently provide data.

I. Introduction
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) uses different accession prefixes to represent distinct record types. GSE denotes a Series (an experiment-level grouping of samples and files), while GDS denotes a curated DataSet. These prefixes are not interchangeable; a single study may have a GSE record and may or may not have a related curated GDS entry.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 represent the same record or interchangeable sources for the same data.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine if GSE309890 and GDS309890 are the same and whether they provide equivalent data access. Hypothesis: they are distinct record types and not interchangeable; the Series (GSE) hosts the processed data files, whereas the curated DataSet (GDS) may not.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We compared the two accessions by querying GEO for each accession’s summary metadata and supplementary file listings, and by resolving each accession to its Entrez UID and FTP directory. GEO-specific tools were selected to avoid ambiguity from generic search.
Materials.
- GEO Series/Record retrieval: functions.geo_series
- GEO accession resolution: functions.geo_resolve_accession
Procedures.
- functions.geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true) to retrieve Series metadata and supplementary files.
- functions.geo_series(accession="GDS309890", list_files=true) to attempt retrieval of GDS metadata and files.
- functions.geo_resolve_accession(accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890") to resolve both to UIDs and FTP directory URLs.
Statistical Analysis.
- Record-type identification and UID were read from the returned fields (entry_type/entry_type_label, uid).
- Sample_count was taken from GSE309890 record’s sample_count field.
- Supplementary_files_count was computed as the length of supplementary_files for each record (denominators: 1 record per accession).
- FTP directory existence was assessed using the presence of the directory path in the tool output and the tool’s note regarding non-existent directories.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Comparison of GEO records for GSE309890 and GDS309890

| Accession   | Entry Type | UID       | Taxon                                      | Platform  | Sample Count | FTP Directory URL                                                             | Supplementary Files Count |
|-------------|------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| GSE309890   | GSE (Series) | 200309890 | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | GPL24659  | 6            | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                 | 1                         |
| GDS309890   | GDS (curated DataSet) | 309890    | [no value returned]                        | [no value returned] | [no value returned] | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/               | 0                         |

Findings.
- GSE309890 is a Series record with UID 200309890, sample_count 6, and one supplementary file (GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz).
- GDS309890 resolves to UID 309890 and an expected GDS FTP path, but the GEO summary returned empty metadata fields and the tool reported no files and a non-existent FTP subdirectory.
- Therefore, GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not the same; only the GSE record currently provides processed expression values.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The results show that GSE309890 is an active Series with accessible processed data, while GDS309890 is a curated DataSet accession without populated metadata or files. They are not the same record and are not interchangeable for data access.
Context. The GSE309890 record contains the study-level grouping and files, including an FPKM matrix. The GDS309890 resolution identifies a curated dataset accession but lacks file registration. The absence of GDS files is consistent with the tool’s note that processed values exist at the Series level.
Limitations. GEO’s API returns metadata only; processed matrices must be downloaded via FTP. The GDS record here reported no files and an empty summary; this does not establish why the curation is absent or whether it may populate later. No PubMed link was registered in GEO for GSE309890 at the time of query.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are distinct. For this study, retrieve expression values via the GSE309890 supplementary FTP file. A future query could re-check GDS309890 for curation updates or explore sample-level (GSM) details if needed. If desired, a downloadable table listing the GSE309890 supplementary files can be generated.

References
[1] NCBI GEO Series record: GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI Entrez esummary call (GSE309890). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0
[3] GEO FTP directory (GSE309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[4] GEO supplementary FTP directory (GSE309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[5] NCBI GEO curated DataSet record: GDS309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[6] NCBI Entrez esummary call (GDS309890). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=309890&version=2.0
[7] GEO FTP directory (GDS309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/
[8] GEO accession resolution (GSE309890, GDS309890). https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ and https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI GEO and Entrez E-utilities for record metadata and FTP directory information.
